findings.reason: §3/§5 should cite `placement.py::ensure_reservation` as the mechanism the exercise demonstrates, not re-plan it, so the node's done-when points at the existing guard (including its "unanswerable queue is not an absent job" rule) instead of a fresh re-hold path.
findings.text: the plan's §3 re-hold done-when ("the next dispatch re-holds the shared allocation") is already implemented by `ensure_reservation`, which is idempotent fleet-wide, replaces a record whose job left the system, and adopts a live supervisor-running allocation (`_adopt_live_fleet_allocation`, reckon/crew/placement.py:488); §5 restates this as work to be built without naming the owner.

findings.reason: §4 should extend and cite `fleet_supervisor.py` rather than describe building the launcher; as written the node would fork the batch step the shipped dependency already owns, and the plan's own stale audit comment ("the launcher ... is not built") is what misleads it.
findings.text: the plan's §4 done-when 1–3 (a batch script starts a zellij server; a session run as its own step keeps its socket under the launcher's runtime directory; ending that step reaps a detached child) are already implemented by `fleet_supervisor.py` (`start_session` :1035, `prepare_runtime` :262, `fleet_supervisor.py:1259`) and tested at `tests/test_fleet_supervisor.py:465` and `:406`.

findings.reason: the honest change is to declare the batch step already carried by `fleet_supervisor.py` and have the cutover exercise it, which removes a whole build node from §4.
findings.text: "The re-hold path ... must create the batch script that starts the zellij server" proposes new build work over a batch step that already exists, with no statement of why `fleet_supervisor.py` cannot be extended.

findings.reason: a reuse map naming `fleet_supervisor.py` and `placement.py::ensure_reservation` would collapse §4's build done-when into "exercise the shipped launcher and re-hold", changing the plan's scope by several nodes.
findings.text: the plan searched the imas-ambix research note and names the baseline's home (imas-ambix `f-shaf-003`), but its reuse search did not reach reckon's own crew code: neither `fleet_supervisor.py` nor `placement.py` is cited anywhere in the plan, and the S21 comment instead claims the launcher is unbuilt.

findings.reason: the plan names no concrete CLI option, MCP view, public definition or refusal family by identifier, so the accounting is implied rather than an added countable; the required edit is covered by the reuse and duplicate findings, not a separate interface decision.
findings.text: §4/§5 add a launcher and a throttled-fraction reader as new machinery without naming what either retires or merges, or why nothing can be; the plan's honest reuse answer (both already owned by `fleet_supervisor.py`/`host.py`) would also be its interface-retirement statement.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the existing owner `fleet_supervisor.py` is one deep module (one module hides zellij start, runtime-dir construction, service supervision and child reaping behind a line protocol); the plan proposes no spread of small wrappers, and its only genuinely new artifact is the single throttled-fraction reader.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3's re-hold proof and §4's launcher/runtime-dir/reaping done-when re-own mechanisms already owned by `reckon/crew/placement.py` (`ensure_reservation`, re-hold, adoption) and `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py` (batch step, runtime dir, reaping), which the plan never names.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §4/§5 add a launcher and a measurement reader (new public surface) without naming what they retire or merge, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched imas-ambix's research note and names the baseline's home, but it does not cite reckon's own `fleet_supervisor.py` or `placement.py`, the code the §4/§5 work would extend, and it presents the batch-step launcher as unbuilt when it shipped.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4 proposes "the launcher" as a new layer over the batch step, but `fleet_supervisor.py` already is that launcher, so building §4 as written produces a parallel wrapper over `start_session`/`prepare_runtime` with no stated reason the existing module cannot be extended.
